criterion: which type of entity the encyclopedia article describes

categories.name: Person
categories.definition: An individual human being, including athletes, politicians, artists, military personnel, and other figures notable for their life and achievements.

categories.name: Building
categories.definition: A man-made structure, such as a tower, school, church, historic house, or other architectural construction.

categories.name: Vehicle
categories.definition: A craft or machine designed for transportation, including automobiles, aircraft, ships, and trains.

categories.name: Album
categories.definition: A collection of audio recordings, such as a music album, EP, or compilation, released as a single item.

categories.name: Educational Institution
categories.definition: An organization dedicated to education, such as a school, college, or university.

categories.name: Animal
categories.definition: A living organism that is a member of the kingdom Animalia, including specific species and genera.

categories.name: Plant
categories.definition: A living organism of the kingdom Plantae, including specific species and genera of flora.

categories.name: Village
categories.definition: A small human settlement or community, typically located in a rural area.

categories.name: Novel
categories.definition: A long work of fiction or literary prose published as a book.

categories.name: Film
categories.definition: A motion picture or movie, including theatrical releases and television films.

categories.name: Company
categories.definition: A business organization or commercial entity formed to trade goods or services.

categories.name: Journal
categories.definition: A periodical academic or professional publication dedicated to a specific field of study.

categories.name: Geographical Feature
categories.definition: A natural physical formation on the Earth's surface, such as a mountain, lake, river, or valley.

categories.name: Book
categories.definition: A written or printed work of non-fiction or a literary collection distinct from a novel.

categories.name: Short Story
categories.definition: A brief work of fiction, typically shorter than a novella or novel.

categories.name: Manga
categories.definition: A Japanese style of comic books or graphic novels.

categories.name: Television Series
categories.definition: A television show consisting of episodes broadcast over a period of time.

categories.name: Newspaper
categories.definition: A printed or digital publication containing news, articles, and advertisements, issued regularly.

categories.name: Magazine
categories.definition: A periodical publication containing articles and illustrations, often covering a specific topic.

categories.name: Record Label
categories.definition: A company that manages brands and trademarks of music recordings and music videos.

categories.name: Arthropod
categories.definition: An invertebrate animal of the phylum Arthropoda, such as an insect, spider, or crustacean.

categories.name: Mollusk
categories.definition: An invertebrate animal of the phylum Mollusca, such as a snail, slug, or octopus.

categories.name: Fungus
categories.definition: A member of the biological kingdom Fungi, such as a mushroom, mold, or yeast.

categories.name: Fictional Character
categories.definition: A person or persona appearing in a work of fiction.

categories.name: Video Game
categories.definition: An electronic game that involves interaction with a user interface to generate visual feedback.

categories.name: Board Game
categories.definition: A tabletop game that involves counters or pieces moved or placed on a pre-marked surface.

categories.name: Sports Team
categories.definition: A group of individuals who play sports together as a unit.

categories.name: Sports Season
categories.definition: A specific period of time during which a sports competition or league takes place.

categories.name: Sports Event
categories.definition: A single or series of athletic competitions, such as a championship or tournament.

categories.name: Award
categories.definition: A prize or recognition given to a person or organization for achievement.

categories.name: Legislative District
categories.definition: A geographical area represented by an elected official in a legislative body.

categories.name: Government Agency
categories.definition: A permanent or semi-permanent organization within a government responsible for the oversight and administration of specific functions.

categories.name: Military Unit
categories.definition: A subdivision of an armed force, such as a division, regiment, or squadron.

categories.name: Military Conflict
categories.definition: A period of armed conflict between two or more groups, such as a war or battle.

categories.name: Political Party
categories.definition: An organized group of people with at least roughly similar political aims and opinions.

categories.name: Language
categories.definition: A system of communication used by a particular country or community.

categories.name: Ethnic Group
categories.definition: A category of people who identify with each other based on common ancestral, social, cultural, or national experience.

categories.name: Religion
categories.definition: A particular system of faith and worship.

categories.name: Disease
categories.definition: A disorder of structure or function in a human, animal, or plant.

categories.name: Chemical Compound
categories.definition: A substance formed when two or more chemical elements are chemically bonded together.

categories.name: Chemical Element
categories.definition: A pure chemical substance consisting of a single type of atom.

categories.name: Scientific Theory
categories.definition: An explanation of an aspect of the natural world and universe that has been repeatedly tested and corroborated.

categories.name: Mathematical Concept
categories.definition: An abstract idea or general notion in the field of mathematics.

categories.name: Physical Constant
categories.definition: A physical quantity that is generally believed to be both universal in nature and have constant value in time.

categories.name: Astronomical Object
categories.definition: A naturally occurring physical entity, association, or structure that exists in the observable universe.

categories.name: Constellation
categories.definition: A group of stars forming a recognizable pattern that is traditionally named after its apparent form or identified with a mythological figure.

categories.name: Zodiac Sign
categories.definition: One of the twelve sectors of the ecliptic plane used in astrology.

categories.name: Geological Period
categories.definition: A subdivision of geological time based on the rock layers and fossil record.

categories.name: Prehistoric Era
categories.definition: A period of time before recorded history.

categories.name: Historical Event
categories.definition: A significant occurrence in the past.

categories.name: Historical Period
categories.definition: An era of history defined by specific cultural, political, or social characteristics.

categories.name: Archaeological Culture
categories.definition: A recurring assemblage of artifacts from a specific time and place that may constitute the material culture remains of a particular past human society.

categories.name: Archaeological Site
categories.definition: A place in which evidence of past activity is preserved, and which has been, or may be, investigated using the discipline of archaeology.

categories.name: Historical Landmark
categories.definition: A building, site, structure, or object that is officially recognized for its historical significance.

categories.name: Museum
categories.definition: A building or place where objects of historical, scientific, artistic, or cultural interest are stored and exhibited.

categories.name: Library
categories.definition: A building or room containing collections of books, periodicals, and sometimes films and recorded music for use or borrowing by the public or the members of an institution.

categories.name: Hospital
categories.definition: An institution providing medical and surgical treatment and nursing care for sick or injured people.

categories.name: Prison
categories.definition: A building to which people are legally committed as a punishment for crimes they have committed or while awaiting trial.

categories.name: Cemetery
categories.definition: A burial ground; a designated area where deceased individuals are interred.

categories.name: Park
categories.definition: A large public green area in a town, used for recreation.

categories.name: Garden
categories.definition: A piece of ground adjoining a house, used for growing flowers, fruit, or vegetables.

categories.name: Zoo
categories.definition: An establishment which maintains a collection of wild animals, typically in a park or gardens, for study, conservation, or display to the public.

categories.name: Aquarium
categories.definition: A building containing an artificial pool or tank of water where live aquatic animals and plants are kept for observation.

categories.name: Stadium
categories.definition: A sports arena with tiers of seats for spectators.

categories.name: Arena
categories.definition: A level area surrounded by seats, in which sports, entertainments, and other public events are held.

categories.name: Theater
categories.definition: A building or outdoor area in which plays and other dramatic performances are given.

categories.name: Restaurant
categories.definition: A place where people pay to sit and eat meals that are cooked and served on the premises.

categories.name: Hotel
categories.definition: An establishment providing accommodation, meals, and other services for travelers and tourists.

categories.name: Bar
categories.definition: An establishment where alcoholic drinks are served.

categories.name: Store
categories.definition: A retail establishment selling items to the public.

categories.name: Market
categories.definition: A regular gathering of people for the purchase and sale of provisions, livestock, and other commodities.

categories.name: Mall
categories.definition: A large building or series of connected buildings containing a variety of retail stores and often restaurants.

categories.name: Airport
categories.definition: A complex of runways and buildings for the takeoff, landing, and maintenance of civil aircraft, with facilities for passengers.

categories.name: Train Station
categories.definition: A place where trains stop to load and unload passengers or goods.

categories.name: Bus Station
categories.definition: A terminal where buses originate, terminate, or stop.

categories.name: Port
categories.definition: A town or city with a harbor where ships load or unload.

categories.name: Bridge
categories.definition: A structure built to carry a road, railway, or path across a river, road, or other obstacle.

categories.name: Tunnel
categories.definition: An artificial underground passage, especially one built through a hill or under a river.

categories.name: Dam
categories.definition: A barrier constructed to hold back water and raise its level, forming a reservoir used to generate electricity or as a water supply.

categories.name: Canal
categories.definition: An artificial waterway constructed to allow the passage of boats or ships inland or to convey water.

categories.name: Road
categories.definition: A wide way leading from one place to another, especially one with a specially prepared surface which vehicles can use.

categories.name: Highway
categories.definition: A main road, especially one connecting major towns or cities.

categories.name: Street
categories.definition: A public road in a city, town, or village, typically with houses and buildings on one or both sides.

categories.name: Square
categories.definition: An open, typically four-sided, area surrounded by buildings in a village, town, or city.

categories.name: Neighborhood
categories.definition: A district or community within a town or city.

categories.name: Suburb
categories.definition: An outlying district of a city, especially a residential one.

categories.name: City
categories.definition: A large town, often with a cathedral or university.

categories.name: Town
categories.definition: An urban area that has a name, defined boundaries, and local government, and that is generally larger than a village and smaller than a city.

categories.name: County
categories.definition: A territorial division of some countries, forming the chief unit of local administration.

categories.name: Province
categories.definition: A principal administrative division of a certain country or region.

categories.name: State
categories.definition: A nation or territory considered as an organized political community under one government.

categories.name: Country
categories.definition: A nation with its own government, occupying a particular territory.

categories.name: Continent
categories.definition: One of the earth's seven main continuous expanses of land.

categories.name: Region
categories.definition: An area, especially part of a country or the world having definable characteristics but not always fixed boundaries.

categories.name: Island
categories.definition: A piece of land surrounded by water.

categories.name: Peninsula
categories.definition: A piece of land almost surrounded by water or projecting out into a body of water.

categories.name: Archipelago
categories.definition: A group of islands.

categories.name: Mountain Range
categories.definition: A line of mountains connected by high ground.

categories.name: Mountain
categories.definition: A large natural elevation of the earth's surface rising abruptly from the surrounding level.

categories.name: Hill
categories.definition: A naturally raised area of land, not as high or craggy as a mountain.

categories.name: Volcano
categories.definition: A mountain or hill, typically conical, having a crater or vent through which lava, rock fragments, hot vapor, and gas are being or have been erupted from the earth's crust.

categories.name: Valley
categories.definition: A low area of land between hills or mountains, typically with a river or stream flowing through it.

categories.name: Canyon
categories.definition: A deep gorge, typically one with a river flowing through it, as found in North America.

categories.name: Cave
categories.definition: A large underground chamber, typically of natural origin, in a hillside or cliff.

categories.name: Waterfall
categories.definition: A cascade of water falling from a height, formed when a river or stream flows over a precipice or steep incline.

categories.name: Lake
categories.definition: A large body of water surrounded by land.

categories.name: River
categories.definition: A large natural stream of water flowing in a channel to the sea, a lake, or another such stream.

categories.name: Stream
categories.definition: A small, narrow river.

categories.name: Spring
categories.definition: A place where water naturally flows out from the ground.

categories.name: Glacier
categories.definition: A slowly moving mass or river of ice formed by the accumulation and compaction of snow on mountains or near the poles.

categories.name: Desert
categories.definition: A dry, barren area of land, typically covered with sand, that receives very little precipitation.

categories.name: Forest
categories.definition: A large area covered chiefly with trees and undergrowth.

categories.name: Jungle
categories.definition: An area of land overgrown with dense forest and tangled vegetation, typically in the tropics.

categories.name: Swamp
categories.definition: An area of low-lying, uncultivated ground where water collects; a bog or marsh.

categories.name: Beach
categories.definition: A pebbly or sandy shore, especially by the ocean between high- and low-water marks.

categories.name: Ocean
categories.definition: A very large expanse of sea, in particular, each of the main areas into which the sea is divided geographically.

categories.name: Sea
categories.definition: The expanse of salt water that covers most of the earth's surface and surrounds its landmasses.

categories.name: Gulf
categories.definition: A deep inlet of the sea almost surrounded by land, with a narrow mouth.

categories.name: Bay
categories.definition: A broad inlet of the sea where the land curves inward.

categories.name: Strait
categories.definition: A narrow passage of water connecting two seas or two other large areas of water.

categories.name: Channel
categories.definition: A length of water wider than a strait, joining two larger areas of water, especially two seas.

categories.name: Cape
categories.definition: A headland or promontory.

categories.name: Atmospheric Phenomenon
categories.definition: A weather event or optical phenomenon that occurs in the atmosphere.

categories.name: Natural Disaster
categories.definition: A natural event such as a flood, earthquake, or hurricane that causes great damage or loss of life.

categories.name: Mineral
categories.definition: A solid inorganic substance of natural occurrence.

categories.name: Rock
categories.definition: The solid mineral material forming part of the surface of the earth and other similar planets.

categories.name: Gemstone
categories.definition: A precious or semi-precious stone, especially when cut and polished.

categories.name: Fossil
categories.definition: The remains or impression of a prehistoric organism preserved in petrified form or as a mold or cast in rock.

categories.name: Ecosystem
categories.definition: A biological community of interacting organisms and their physical environment.

categories.name: Biome
categories.definition: A large naturally occurring community of flora and fauna occupying a major habitat, e.g. forest or tundra.

categories.name: Habitat
categories.definition: The natural home or environment of an animal, plant, or other organism.

categories.name: Food
categories.definition: Any substance consumed to provide nutritional support for an organism.

categories.name: Drink
categories.definition: A liquid that can be swallowed as refreshment or nourishment.

categories.name: Clothing
categories.definition: Items worn to cover the body.

categories.name: Furniture
categories.definition: The movable articles that are used to make a room or other building suitable for living or working.

categories.name: Tool
categories.definition: A device or implement, especially one held in the hand, used to carry out a particular function.

categories.name: Instrument
categories.definition: A device for producing musical sounds or for scientific or navigational purposes.

categories.name: Weapon
categories.definition: A thing designed or used for inflicting bodily harm or physical damage.

categories.name: Toy
categories.definition: An object for a child to play with, typically a model or miniature replica of something.

categories.name: Currency
categories.definition: A system of money in general use in a particular country.

categories.name: Stock Market Index
categories.definition: A measurement of the value of a section of the stock market.

categories.name: Product
categories.definition: An article or substance that is manufactured or refined for sale.

categories.name: Brand
categories.definition: A type of product manufactured by a particular company under a particular name.

categories.name: Software
categories.definition: Programs and other operating information used by a computer.

categories.name: Website
categories.definition: A location connected to the Internet that maintains one or more pages on the World Wide Web.

categories.name: Programming Language
categories.definition: A formal language comprising a set of instructions that produce various kinds of output.

categories.name: File Format
categories.definition: A standard way that information is encoded for storage in a computer file.

categories.name: Algorithm
categories.definition: A process or set of rules to be followed in calculations or other problem-solving operations, especially by a computer.

categories.name: Protocol
categories.definition: A set of rules governing the exchange or transmission of data between devices.

categories.name: Standard
categories.definition: A required or agreed level of quality or attainment.

categories.name: Unit of Measurement
categories.definition: A definite magnitude of a quantity, defined and adopted by convention or by law, that is used as a standard for measurement of the same kind of quantity.

categories.name: Color
categories.definition: The property possessed by an object of producing different sensations on the eye as a result of the way it reflects or emits light.

categories.name: Shape
categories.definition: The external form or appearance characteristic of someone or something.

categories.name: Number
categories.definition: An arithmetical value, expressed by a word, symbol, or figure, representing a particular quantity.

categories.name: Symbol
categories.definition: A mark, character, or object used as a conventional representation of an object, function, or process.

categories.name: Letter
categories.definition: A character representing one or more of the sounds used in speech; any of the symbols of an alphabet.

categories.name: Punctuation Mark
categories.definition: A mark used to separate sentences and clarify meaning, such as a period or comma.

categories.name: Word
categories.definition: A single distinct meaningful element of speech or writing.

categories.name: Phrase
categories.definition: A small group of words standing together as a conceptual unit.

categories.name: Idiom
categories.definition: A group of words established by usage as having a meaning not deducible from those of the individual words.

categories.name: Proverb
categories.definition: A short pithy saying in general use, stating a general truth or piece of advice.

categories.name: Quote
categories.definition: A repetition of someone else's statement or thoughts.

categories.name: Joke
categories.definition: A thing that someone says to cause amusement or laughter.

categories.name: Riddle
categories.definition: A question or statement intentionally phrased so as to require ingenuity in ascertaining its answer or meaning.

categories.name: Myth
categories.definition: A traditional story, especially one concerning the early history of a people or explaining some natural or social phenomenon.

categories.name: Legend
categories.definition: A traditional story sometimes regarded as historical but unauthenticated.

categories.name: Fairy Tale
categories.definition: A children's story about magical and imaginary beings and lands.

categories.name: Folklore
categories.definition: The traditional beliefs, customs, and stories of a community, passed through the generations by word of mouth.

categories.name: Deity
categories.definition: A god or goddess in a polytheistic religion.

categories.name: Demon
categories.definition: An evil spirit or devil, especially one thought to possess a person or act as a tormentor in hell.

categories.name: Angel
categories.definition: A spiritual being believed to act as an attendant, agent, or messenger of God.

categories.name: Saint
categories.definition: A person acknowledged as holy or virtuous and typically regarded as being in heaven after death.

categories.name: Prophet
categories.definition: A person regarded as an inspired teacher or proclaimer of the will of God.

categories.name: Pope
categories.definition: The Bishop of Rome as head of the Roman Catholic Church.

categories.name: Monarch
categories.definition: A sovereign head of state, especially a king, queen, or emperor.

categories.name: Noble Title
categories.definition: A rank or status held by a person of high social or political importance.

categories.name: Order of Chivalry
categories.definition: A society of knights founded by a sovereign or other person of high rank.

categories.name: Award
categories.definition: A prize or other mark of recognition given in honor of an achievement.

categories.name: Treaty
categories.definition: A formally concluded and ratified agreement between countries.

categories.name: Law
categories.definition: The system of rules which a particular country or community recognizes as regulating the actions of its members and which it may enforce by the imposition of penalties.

categories.name: Court Case
categories.definition: A legal dispute between two or more parties that is decided by a court.

categories.name: Constitution
categories.definition: A body of fundamental principles or established precedents according to which a state or other organization is acknowledged to be governed.

categories.name: Election
categories.definition: A formal and organized process of electing or being elected, especially of members of a political body.

categories.name: Summit
categories.definition: A meeting between heads of government.

categories.name: Protest
categories.definition: A statement or action expressing disapproval of or objection to something.

categories.name: Strike
categories.definition: A refusal to work organized by a body of employees as a form of protest.

categories.name: Revolution
categories.definition: A forcible overthrow of a government or social order, in favor of a new system.

categories.name: Coup
categories.definition: A sudden, violent, and illegal seizure of power from a government.

categories.name: Assassination
categories.definition: The murder of an important person in a surprise attack for political or religious reasons.

categories.name: Terrorist Attack
categories.definition: A violent act or threat of violence intended to create fear and achieve a political, religious, or ideological goal.

categories.name: Mass Shooting
categories.definition: An incident involving multiple victims of gun violence.

categories.name: Kidnapping
categories.definition: The action of abducting someone and holding them captive.

categories.name: Robbery
categories.definition: The action of robbing a person or place.

categories.name: Fraud
categories.definition: Wrongful or criminal deception intended to result in financial or personal gain.

categories.name: Scandal
categories.definition: An action or event regarded as morally or legally wrong and causing general public outrage.

categories.name: Disappearance
categories.definition: An instance or fact of someone or something ceasing to be visible or present.

categories.name: Rescue
categories.definition: An act of saving or being saved from danger or difficulty.

categories.name: Discovery
categories.definition: The action or process of discovering or being discovered.

categories.name: Invention
categories.definition: The action of inventing something, typically a process or device.

categories.name: Exploration
categories.definition: The action of traveling in or through an unfamiliar area in order to learn about it.

categories.name: Expedition
categories.definition: A journey undertaken by a group of people with a particular purpose, especially that of exploration, research, or war.

categories.name: Mission
categories.definition: An important assignment carried out for political, religious, or commercial purposes, typically involving travel.

categories.name: Project
categories.definition: An individual or collaborative enterprise that is carefully planned and designed to achieve a particular aim.

categories.name: Construction
categories.definition: The building of something, typically a large structure.

categories.name: Demolition
categories.definition: The action or process of demolishing or being demolished.

categories.name: Renovation
categories.definition: The action of renovating a building or structure.

categories.name: Opening
categories.definition: The action or process of opening something.

categories.name: Closing
categories.definition: The action or process of closing something.

categories.name: Launch
categories.definition: The action of launching something, such as a ship or a product.

categories.name: Crash
categories.definition: A violent collision, typically of one vehicle with another or with an obstacle.

categories.name: Explosion
categories.definition: A violent and destructive shattering or blowing apart of something, as is caused by a bomb.

categories.name: Fire
categories.definition: Combustion or burning, in which substances combine chemically with oxygen from the air and typically give out bright light, heat, and smoke.

categories.name: Flood
categories.definition: An overflow of a large amount of water beyond its normal limits, especially over what is normally dry land.

categories.name: Earthquake
categories.definition: A sudden and violent shaking of the ground, sometimes causing great destruction, as a result of movements within the earth's crust or volcanic action.

categories.name: Hurricane
categories.definition: A storm with a violent wind, in particular a tropical cyclone in the Caribbean.

categories.name: Tornado
categories.definition: A mobile, destructive vortex of violently rotating winds having the appearance of a funnel-shaped cloud and advancing beneath a large storm system.

categories.name: Volcanic Eruption
categories.definition: The sudden occurrence of a violent discharge of steam and volcanic material.

categories.name: Tsunami
categories.definition: A long, high sea wave caused by a disturbance, such as an earthquake or volcanic eruption.

categories.name: Drought
categories.definition: A prolonged period of abnormally low rainfall, leading to a shortage of water.

categories.name: Famine
categories.definition: Extreme scarcity of food.

categories.name: Epidemic
categories.definition: A widespread occurrence of an infectious disease in a community at a particular time.

categories.name: Pandemic
categories.definition: An outbreak of a disease that occurs over a wide geographic area and affects an exceptionally high proportion of the population.

categories.name: Plague
categories.definition: A contagious bacterial disease characterized by fever and delirium, typically with the formation of buboes.

categories.name: Outbreak
categories.definition: The sudden or violent start of something unwelcome, such as war or disease.

categories.name: Accident
categories.definition: An unfortunate incident that happens unexpectedly and unintentionally, typically resulting in damage or injury.

categories.name: Disaster
categories.definition: A sudden event, such as an accident or a natural catastrophe, that causes great damage or loss of life.

categories.name: Emergency
categories.definition: A serious, unexpected, and often dangerous situation requiring immediate action.

categories.name: Crisis
categories.definition: A time of intense difficulty, trouble, or danger.

categories.name: Conflict
categories.definition: A serious disagreement or argument, typically a protracted one.

categories.name: War
categories.definition: A state of armed conflict between different nations or states or different groups within a nation or state.

categories.name: Battle
categories.definition: A sustained fight between large organized armed forces.

categories.name: Siege
categories.definition: A military operation in which enemy forces surround a town or building, cutting off essential supplies, compelling those inside to surrender.

categories.name: Invasion
categories.definition: An instance of invading a country or region with an armed force.

categories.name: Occupation
categories.definition: The action, state, or period of occupying or being occupied by military force.

categories.name: Revolt
categories.definition: Take violent action against an established government or ruler.

categories.name: Uprising
categories.definition: An act of resistance or rebellion; a revolt.

categories.name: Rebellion
categories.definition: The action or process of resisting authority, control, or convention.

categories.name: Civil War
categories.definition: A war between citizens of the same country.

categories.name: World War
categories.definition: A war involving many large nations in all different parts of the world.

categories.name: Cold War
categories.definition: A state of political hostility between countries characterized by threats, propaganda, and other measures short of open warfare.

categories.name: Genocide
categories.definition: The deliberate killing of a large group of people, especially those of a particular ethnic group or nation.

categories.name: Holocaust
categories.definition: The mass murder of Jews under the German Nazi regime during the period 1941–45.

categories.name: Massacre
categories.definition: An indiscriminate and brutal slaughter of people.

categories.name: Execution
categories.definition: The carrying out of a sentence of death on a condemned person.

categories.name: Assassination
categories.definition: The murder of an important person in a surprise attack for political or religious reasons.

categories.name: Murder
categories.definition: The unlawful premeditated killing of one human being by another.

categories.name: Homicide
categories.definition: The killing of one person by another.

categories.name: Suicide
categories.definition: The action of killing oneself intentionally.

categories.name: Death
categories.definition: The action or fact of dying or being killed; the end of the life of a person or organism.

categories.name: Funeral
categories.definition: A ceremony held in connection with the burial or cremation of a dead person.

categories.name: Memorial
categories.definition: A structure or monument erected in memory of a person or event.

categories.name: Cemetery
categories.definition: A burial ground; a designated area where deceased individuals are interred.

categories.name: Grave
categories.definition: A place of burial for a dead body, typically a hole dug in the ground.

categories.name: Tomb
categories.definition: A large vault, typically an underground one, for burying the dead.

categories.name: Mausoleum
categories.definition: A stately or impressive building housing a tomb or group of tombs.

categories.name: Catacomb
categories.definition: An underground cemetery consisting of a subterranean gallery with recesses for tombs.

categories.name: Cremation
categories.definition: The burning of a dead body.

categories.name: Burial
categories.definition: The action or practice of interring a dead body.

categories.name: Mourning
categories.definition: The expression of deep sorrow for someone who has died.

categories.name: Grief
categories.definition: Deep sorrow, especially that caused by someone's death.

categories.name: Loss
categories.definition: The fact or process of losing something or someone.

categories.name: Tragedy
categories.definition: An event causing great suffering, destruction, and distress, such as a serious accident, crime, or natural catastrophe.

categories.name: Miracle
categories.definition: A surprising and welcome event that is not explicable by natural or scientific laws and is therefore attributed to a divine agency.

categories.name: Wonder
categories.definition: A feeling of surprise mingled with admiration, caused by something beautiful, unexpected, unfamiliar, or inexplicable.

categories.name: Mystery
categories.definition: Something that is difficult or impossible to understand or explain.

categories.name: Secret
categories.definition: Something that is kept or meant to be kept unknown or unseen by others.

categories.name: Rumor
categories.definition: A currently circulating story or report of uncertain or doubtful truth.

categories.name: Gossip
categories.definition: Casual or unconstrained conversation or reports about other people, typically involving details that are not confirmed as being true.

categories.name: News
categories.definition: Newly received or noteworthy information, especially about recent or important events.

categories.name: Report
categories.definition: A spoken or written account of something that one has observed, heard, done, or investigated.

categories.name: Article
categories.definition: A piece of writing included with others in a newspaper, magazine, or other publication.

categories.name: Story
categories.definition: An account of imaginary or real people and events told for entertainment.

categories.name: Narrative
categories.definition: A spoken or written account of connected events; a story.

categories.name: Tale
categories.definition: A fictitious or true incident or story.

categories.name: Legend
categories.definition: A traditional story sometimes regarded as historical but unauthenticated.

categories.name: Myth
categories.definition: A traditional story, especially one concerning the early history of a people or explaining some natural or social phenomenon.

categories.name: Fable
categories.definition: A short story, typically with animals as characters, conveying a moral.

categories.name: Parable
categories.definition: A simple story used to illustrate a moral or spiritual lesson.

categories.name: Allegory
categories.definition: A story, poem, or picture that can be interpreted to reveal a hidden meaning, typically a moral or political one.

categories.name: Satire
categories.definition: The use of humor, irony, exaggeration, or ridicule to expose and criticize people's stupidity or vices.

categories.name: Irony
categories.definition: The expression of one's meaning by using language that normally signifies the opposite, typically for humorous or emphatic effect.

categories.name: Metaphor
categories.definition: A figure of speech in which a word or phrase is applied to an object or action to which it is not literally applicable.

categories.name: Simile
categories.definition: A figure of speech involving the comparison of one thing with another thing of a different kind, used to make a description more emphatic or vivid.

categories.name: Hyperbole
categories.definition: Exaggerated statements or claims not meant to be taken literally.

categories.name: Oxymoron
categories.definition: A figure of speech in which apparently contradictory terms appear in conjunction.

categories.name: Paradox
categories.definition: A statement that seems self-contradictory or absurd but in reality expresses a possible truth.

categories.name: Pun
categories.definition: A joke exploiting the different possible meanings of a word or the fact that there are words that sound alike but have different meanings.

categories.name: Joke
categories.definition: A thing that someone says to cause amusement or laughter.

categories.name: Riddle
categories.definition: A question or statement intentionally phrased so as to require ingenuity in ascertaining its answer or meaning.

categories.name: Limerick
categories.definition: A humorous, frequently bawdy, verse of three long and two short lines rhyming aabba.

categories.name: Haiku
categories.definition: A Japanese poem of seventeen syllables, in three lines of five, seven, and five, traditionally evoking images of the natural world.

categories.name: Sonnet
categories.definition: A poem of fourteen lines using any of a number of formal rhyme schemes, in English typically having ten syllables per line.

categories.name: Poem
categories.definition: A piece of writing in which the expression of feelings and ideas is given intensity by the use of distinctive style and rhythm.

categories.name: Song
categories.definition: A short poem or other set of words set to music or meant to be sung.

categories.name: Hymn
categories.definition: A religious song or poem of praise to God or a god.

categories.name: Anthem
categories.definition: A rousing or uplifting song identified with a particular group, body, or cause.

categories.name: Ballad
categories.definition: A poem or song narrating a story in short stanzas.

categories.name: Epic
categories.definition: A long poem, typically one derived from ancient oral tradition, narrating the deeds and adventures of heroic or legendary figures or the history of a nation.

categories.name: Novel
categories.definition: A fictitious prose narrative of book length, typically representing character and action with some degree of realism.

categories.name: Short Story
categories.definition: A story with a fully developed theme but significantly shorter and less elaborate than a novel.
